newsitem.title: UK: UK Sumitomo investigators await contempt judgment.
newsitem.headline: UK Sumitomo investigators await contempt judgment.

text.p: Judgment was reserved in a contempt of court case on Wednesday against Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) over its investigation of the Sumitomo Corp copper scandal.

Two judges reserved judgment on the landmark high court action brought by a firm of accountants against five SFO officials who could in theory be sentenced to prison. Judgment may be made on Thursday.

Counsel for the firm of Kay Accountants Ltd which was raided by the SFO on December 6 has alleged that the agency seized computers, and then in breach of a court order milked information from them and failed to return them.
The proceedings were to have been run in tandem with an application for a judicial review of the original search and seize warrants granted to the SFO by London magistrates.
But on Wednesday the judicial review moves were put on legal hold by Lord Justice Staughton and Justice Scott Baker, pending a decision on the contempt case.
The SFO officials are director George Staple, lawyers Andrew Jackson and Christopher Walker, accountant Anne Dilks and computer expert Michael Hainey.
The SFO, in liaison with investigators in Japan and the United States, is is investigating the multi-billion dollar scandal that rocked world metal markets in June last year.

Japanese conglomerate Sumitomo fired its head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he was a rogue who admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading. --London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
